title: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: params, streaming, and function-call surface updates
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Bring Redwood's /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer closer to OpenAI semantics so downstream customers can switch clients with fewer surface differences. This PR standardizes parameter names/behavior (stop, logprobs, max_tokens, top_p, presence/frequency penalty), converges role mapping for multi-turn chats, improves streaming stability and reconnect semantics, and extends function/tool-calling wiring to match OpenAI's function_call + arguments patterns. Checklist: - [x] Parameter aliases and validation (openai-style names) - [x] Streaming delta/frame semantics and boundary markers - [x] Response formatting: choices[].message and choices[].delta compatibility - [x] function_call and tool invocation plumbing + deterministic fallback - [x] Tests for stop sequence handling and logprobs shape - [x] Docs snips and SDK examples updated (Python + TS) Summary of changes: 1) API surface: added compatibility aliases so clients can send either Redwood-native names or OpenAI names (e.g. temperature/temperature, topP/top_p, maxTokens/max_tokens). Validation layer now rejects contradictory fields (e.g. both "n" and "best_of" in same request) and returns clear 4xx messages. 2) Roles: normalized roles mapping to accept OpenAI roles (system, user, assistant) and preserve additional role metadata; conversation encoder now preserves explicit role ordering for multi-turn context windows to avoid implicit reordering regressions. 3) stop & logprobs: implemented stop sequence handling identical to OpenAI (applies to all completions and streaming), exposing logprobs when requested and ensuring token index alignment in returned choices[].logprobs; missing logits now return nulls rather than silently dropping fields. 4) Streaming stability: improved chunk delimiting and heartbeat frames; server will emit a STREAM_READY delta once per stream and include a final DONE sentinel with consistent JSON framing so client libraries can resynchronize after transient connection resets. Added exponential reconnect hints in the stream metadata and made the stream idempotent for at-least-once reconnects. 5) Function/tool-calling: support for OpenAI's function_call objects was added. When a function_call is returned, choices[].message.function_call will include name and arguments string (stringified JSON) and the platform will surface the function's JSON schema in the model metadata so clients can perform local validation. Tool execution hooks added to the runtime that accept pull-based invocations (call -> exec -> return-to-chat). 6) Response formatting and structured output: introduced content-type hinting and explicit structured output envelopes for models that return JSON objects. This reduces heuristic text parsing on the client. 7) SDK & docs: small compat examples added to redwood-sdk-python and redwood-sdk-typescript showing stream consumption, function_call handling, and logprobs post-processing. Known limitations: - logprobs for heavily-quantized models may be approximate; clients should treat them as diagnostic. - function_call argument strings are not guaranteed to be pretty-printed. Notes and references: sees-ENG-4321 for product acceptance criteria; related infra change in ENG-4389 for stream proxy buffering. Links: RFC for streaming framing: https://internal.redwood.ai/rfc/stream-framing, product ticket: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4321/openai-compatibility

review_comments: Arjun Patel: overall this looks good; one request: make streaming DONE sentinel idempotent so clients can safely ack and not reapply function calls if reconnect occurs.
Maya Chen (author): addressed above; added sentinel idempotency token and updated tool_dispatcher to track idempotency across reconnects.
Lena García: small nit on param validation error codes — prefer 422 for semantic conflicts vs 400 for malformed. Updated validator to return 422 with a machine-friendly error_code key.
Connor Lee: CI flaky streaming test failed on first run (timeout) but passed on rerun; added a 2s buffer in the test harness to account for noisy CI nodes.
QA (internal): confirmed that stop sequences are honored for multi-segment responses and that logprobs array lengths match returned tokens in both streaming and non-streaming modes.
release_notes: Added OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer improvements: parameter aliases, normalized roles, streaming framing stability (STREAM_READY/DONE sentinels), function_call support, structured output envelopes, and updated SDK examples. No breaking changes expected.
notes_for_ops: Operators: the streaming proxy buffer size must be increased to 8MB in older clusters to avoid partial-frame drops when models emit large initial system prompts. Apply helm chart values in charts/values/openai-compat-values.yaml. Monitor new metric 'streaming.frames.dropped' and alert if >5/min for 5m.
testing_summary: Unit tests added for param validation and function_call plumbing. Integration tests cover stop sequences/logprobs in non-streaming and streaming modes. E2E test simulates reconnect scenarios and verifies idempotent function_call semantics. CI initially had one flaky streaming test; reran and adjusted harness timing.
